Physics 1 Review - Fluids

Fluid Statics vs. Fluid Dynamics

Fluid statics is the study of fluids at rest. Fluid dynamics is the study of fluids in motion.

Pressure

Pressure is defined as P=F⊥AP=F⊥A.

need figure of force perpendicular acting on an area

Atmospheric pressure maybe expressed in various units: 

        Patm = 1.01x105 N/m2 = 101kPa = 14.7 lb/in2 = 1 bar

 

Gauge pressure (Pg) is the difference between absolute pressure and atmospheric pressure or

Pg = Pabs - Patm.

 

Tire pressure often stated on the driver's door as a value near 35 Lb/in2 is a gauge pressure:

Pgauge = Pabs - Patm = 49.7Lb/in2 - 14.7Lb/in2 = 35Lb/in2

Pascal's Principal

Pascal's Principle states that an external pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted unchanged to every point within the fluid.

The figure below shows a hydraulic lift.

 

Thus

Pout=PinPout=Pin  or    FoutAout=FinAinFoutAout=FinAin.

 

Archimedes' Principal and Buoyancy

The figures below show masses in fluids.

Archimedes' Principle states that an object immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the displaced fluid (DF).

 

Thus FB = WDF = mDFg = ρDFρDF Vg

Summing forces on the mass in the y-direction gives:                            FB−Fg=mayFB−Fg=may

If ay = 0 then:

FB=FgFB=Fg
